steps.title: Writing used to begin with a blank page
say: Alex’s first task at Contoso was an executive proposal for the AI Customer Support Platform.
Without Copilot that’s four passes — research, write, rewrite, review — and the first one starts from nothing.
With Copilot it’s three: prompt, refine, approve. The first pass already has words in it.
Copilot removes the blank page. It doesn’t remove the judgement — Alex still decides what the proposal says.

steps.title: The deck came out of the document Alex had already written
say: The steering committee needed slides, and the proposal was already finished. So why start again?
The slow path opens an empty deck — create from scratch, format the slides, build the visuals, format them again.
Copilot in PowerPoint builds the presentation from Proposal dot docx, on Contoso’s own template.
It doesn’t invent the story, it reuses the one Alex already wrote. What’s left is editing a real deck instead of starting one.

steps.title: Alex asked the spreadsheet a question
say: Eighteen months of support tickets, across six regions.
The old order is to build the model first — pivot tables, complex formulas, manual analysis — and ask the question afterwards.
With Copilot the question comes first, in plain English. Which region drove the September spike? EMEA — with password resets the biggest category behind the rise.
You no longer have to know the formula to reach the insight. Alex still checks the numbers.

steps.title: Three hundred unread, and a decision buried in them
say: Alex came back to an inbox that had carried on without them — three hundred unread, one project thread somewhere in the middle of it.
Without Copilot the only route through is to read every message before answering any of them.
With Copilot the thread is read once, in summary, and the reply is drafted from it — using only mail Alex could already open.
Reading the inbox was never the job. Deciding is — and nothing sends until Alex has approved it.

steps.title: The meeting was worked once, not twice
say: The steering committee ran for an hour, recorded and transcribed.
Without Copilot that hour gets spent twice — typing notes instead of contributing, then scrubbing back through the recording for who agreed to what.
With Copilot the recap, the action items and the next steps come out of the transcript as the meeting ends.
Nobody has to be the note-taker instead of a participant.

steps.title: Delegated work
say: Getting the pilot ready meant chasing threads, finding a meeting slot, drafting a brief, writing an invite, and sending it all out.
Without Cowork, that's five chores, each one started and finished by hand.
With Copilot Cowork, it's one request. Alex describes the goal, approves what goes out, and reviews the result.
Cowork does the legwork. Alex keeps the decisions.

steps.title: This is the difference Copilot actually makes
say: Six apps, one project, one month at Contoso — and one assistant behind all of it.
Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook, Teams and Copilot Chat, as one experience across every app Alex already had open.
Microsoft 365 is where people create the work. Microsoft 365 Copilot helps them understand, create, analyse, communicate and act faster using the work that’s already there.
The value isn’t the AI. It’s what the AI does with the work you already had — and Alex is still the one deciding.
